acceptedAnswer.text: One Komboe account syncs the web vault, browser extensions, phone, desktop, command line and the assistant. You sign in with your email and master password, and you can add a passkey and two-step login.

mainEntity.name: Does Komboe ever see my master password?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. The home page and the web vault hash the master password on the device. Only that hash is sent, and the vault is encrypted before it syncs.

mainEntity.name: Can an admin reset my master password?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. There is no backdoor and no admin password reset. Keep your recovery kit safe.

mainEntity.name: Does this website ask for my password?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. The home page sign-in form uses the same flow as the web vault, including a two-step code when the account has one. The password stays in the browser and is not stored on this site.

Self-hosted servers use local Komboe accounts by default. Organizations can optionally add enterprise single sign-on. Vault decryption still needs each person's master password. A self-hosted Komboe server does not contact Komboe. Outside services stay off unless you turn them on. Desktop and CLI update checks stay off until you point them at a feed you host. A breach check runs only when you ask for it. Password checks send only a k-anonymity hash prefix, never the password. The data breach report sends your email address to your Komboe server, which forwards it only if the operator has configured a breach-check key. The web vault uses the server it was loaded from. Until you save a server URL, some apps still have a cloud default compiled in. Set your server URL when you first sign in.
